#33926
STAT 157 001 - SEM 001 offered through Statistics
section closed

Seminar on Topics in Probability and Statistics

Statistical Foundations of Modern AI
Jingfeng Wu
Jan 19, 2027 - May 07, 2027
Tu, Th
09:30 am - 10:59 am
Hildebrand B51
Class #:33926
Units:3

Instruction Mode: In-Person Instruction

No Open Seats
This seminar explores the statistical and mathematical foundations of modern artificial intelligence, with an emphasis on optimization and generalization in machine learning and deep learning. Using linear models and simple neural networks, we will study how learning algorithms fit data and how choices such as model size, initialization, learning rate, and training time affect predictive performance. Topics include gradient descent, overparameterization, and explicit and implicit regularization. Selected further topics may include scaling laws and in-context learning. The course combines mathematical analysis, computational experiments, and guided readings, with substantial student participation through discussion, presentations, and a final project. Prerequisites: Multivariable calculus (MATH 53), linear algebra (MATH 54 or 56), and probability (STAT 134, DATA/STAT C140, or EECS 126), or equivalent preparation. Basic Python programming and comfort with mathematical reasoning are expected. Prior coursework in machine learning, such as STAT 154 or CS 189, is strongly recommended.

Probability and Risk Analysis for Engineers

Thibaut Mastrolia
Jan 19, 2027 - May 07, 2027
Tu, Th
05:00 pm - 06:29 pm
Cory 277
Class #:29078
Units:4

Instruction Mode: In-Person Instruction

Open Seats

This is an introductory course in probability designed to develop a good understanding of uncertain phenomena and the mathematical tools used to model and analyze it. Applications will be given in such areas as reliability theory, risk theory, inventory theory, financial models, and computer science, among others. This course is a probability course and cannot be used to fulfill any engineering unit or elective requirements.
